prompt: How do I transcribe a meeting in Teams?
completion:
### Quick‑Start: Transcribing a Teams Meeting

| What you’ll need | Why it matters |
|------------------|----------------|
| **A Teams account** in a subscription that supports transcription (Office 365 / Microsoft 365, Enterprise/Education, or Teams for Business). | Transcription is a premium feature that isn’t available in the free consumer tier. |
| **Admin rights (or a meeting policy that allows transcription)** | Only people who can enable the feature can start it. |
| **Teams client** (desktop or web) **updated to the latest version** | The “Start transcription” button appears in newer releases. |
| **A meeting host/organizer** | Only the host can start transcription. |

Once those conditions are met, you can start transcription in a meeting in just a few clicks. Below is a step‑by‑step guide that covers both the *meeting‑time* actions and the *admin‑side* configuration.

---

## 1. Make Sure Transcription Is Enabled for Your Organization

### 1.1 Admin Center

1. **Log in** to the Microsoft 365 admin center (`admin.microsoft.com`).
2. In the left pane, click **Teams** → **Meetings** → **Meeting policies**.
3. Pick the policy you want to apply to the user(s) (e.g., “Global (Org default)”).
4. **Toggle on** the setting “Allow transcription”.
5. **Save** the policy.

> **Tip:** If you’re using a custom policy, you’ll have to edit that policy instead of the default.

### 1.2 Individual User Settings

If you’re a meeting host who isn’t an admin, you can also toggle transcription from your Teams client:

1. Click **…** (More options) in the top right of the Teams app.
2. Go to **Settings** → **Calls** → **Allow transcription**.  
   (If you don’t see it, the policy is probably turned off by your admin.)

---

## 2. Start Transcribing During a Meeting

> **Prerequisites:** You must be the meeting host or have the host role.  
> **Supported languages:** English (U.S. & U.K.), Spanish, French, German, Italian, and a handful of others. The default is the language of the Teams client.

### 2.1 Desktop App (Windows / macOS)

1. **Join** or **start** the meeting as usual.
2. Click the **…** (More options) in the meeting controls bar.
3. Select **Start transcription**.
4. A pop‑up will appear: “Transcription started. The transcript will appear in the meeting chat.”
5. The transcript scrolls in real time next to the chat pane. Participants can click on any line to jump to that portion of the audio.

### 2.2 Web App

1. Join the meeting in the Teams web client (Chrome, Edge, or Safari).
2. Click **…** → **Start transcription** exactly as you would in the desktop app.
3. The transcript appears in the chat pane, same as the desktop version.

### 2.3 Mobile App

> **Current limitation:** The mobile Teams app (iOS/Android) does not support live transcription.  
> **Workaround:** Start the transcription on a desktop or web client and the transcript will be available to everyone in the chat (including mobile users) once the meeting ends.

---

## 3. Managing the Transcript After the Meeting

### 3.1 During the Meeting

- **Pause / Resume**: Click the “Pause transcription” button (the same as “Start transcription” but with a pause icon).  
- **End**: Click **End transcription**. The transcript stops updating but remains in the chat.

### 3.2 After the Meeting

1. **Automatic Save**: When the meeting ends, Teams saves the transcript file (`.vtt`) to the meeting's **recording folder** in **OneDrive** (for the host) or **SharePoint** (for channel meetings).
2. **Access the transcript**:
   - Open the chat thread from the meeting. The transcript will appear under the “Files” tab.
   - Or navigate to the OneDrive/SharePoint folder (usually `MeetingName` → `Transcript`).
3. **Download / Edit**:
   - Click **Download** → **Download transcript** to save a `.vtt` or `.txt` file locally.
   - Open the file in any text editor or use the “Open in Teams” button to view the transcript directly in Teams.

> **Note:** Transcripts are searchable and can be used for compliance or record‑keeping purposes. Keep in mind the privacy policy of your organization.

---

## 4. Common Issues & How to Fix Them

| Problem | Likely Cause | Quick Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| “Start transcription” button missing | Admin policy disabled | Ask your Teams admin to enable transcription. |
| Transcription doesn’t appear in chat | Meeting isn’t recorded | In some environments, transcription is only available when the meeting is also recorded. Try “Start recording” first. |
| Audio isn’t being captured in the transcript | Poor microphone or background noise | Use a dedicated mic and minimize background noise; check audio input settings. |
| Transcription language wrong | Teams client language set to something else | Change the Teams client language: Settings → General → Language. |
| Transcript appears only for host | Only hosts can start transcription | The host must start it; participants cannot. |

---

## 5. Tips for Making the Most of Transcripts

- **Label speakers**: Teams automatically tags speakers with their names, but you can manually edit the transcript afterward if you want to correct a misidentified speaker.
- **Search in chat**: Use the chat’s search bar to find specific words or phrases from the transcript instantly.
- **Combine with recording**: Recording gives you the video/audio, while transcription gives you searchable text. Most Teams users turn both on for complete documentation.
- **Export to Word**: Copy the transcript text from chat or the downloaded file and paste it into a Word doc for easier editing or formatting.
- **Legal Holds**: If you’re under a legal hold or e‑Discovery requirement, the transcript will be preserved along with the meeting recording and chat.

---

## 6. Quick Checklist

- [ ] Admin policy: **Allow transcription** is turned on.  
- [ ] Host has the **Host** role (or is the meeting organizer).  
- [ ] Teams app is **updated**.  
- [ ] During meeting: **Click “Start transcription”** in the meeting controls.  
- [ ] After meeting: **Locate transcript** in chat or OneDrive/SharePoint.  
- [ ] **Download** or **share** the transcript as needed.

That’s it! With these steps you’ll have a fully transcribed record of your Teams meeting—ready to search, share, or archive. Happy meeting!
